Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:10:1.hebrew: בבייתוס שמנה נביאים - כל ספרי נביאים שמנה הן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:10:1.english: Boethus [that] the Prophets are eight - All the books of the Prophets are eight.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:11:1.hebrew: ה"ג וכן בין כל נביא ונביא, ובנביא של שנים עשר שלש שיטין, ומסיים מלמטה ומתחיל מלמעלה - אם נזדמן לו סיום הספר מלמטה בסוף הדף, מתחיל ספרו האחר בראש הדף, ואינו צריך להניח ריוח חלק ביניהם:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:11:1.english: The reading is: "And so too between each prophet and the next, and in the [book of the] Twelve Prophets, three lines" - and he finishes at the bottom and begins at the top: If the end of the book happens to fall at the bottom, at the end of the page, he begins his other book at the top of the page, and he does not need to leave a blank space between them.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:12:1.hebrew: כדי לגול עמוד - מניח קלף חלק לגלול על גבי עמוד של עץ שהספר נגלל עליו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:12:1.english: Enough to wind around the column - He leaves a blank parchment [sheet] to wind around the wooden column upon which the book is rolled.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:12:2.hebrew: וסופו כדי לגול היקף - בסופו מניח חלק גדול כדי לגול בו כל הקיפו, שאין עושה שני עמודים לגוללו לאמצעו כמו שאנו עושין לספר תורה, אלא גוללו מתחלתו לסופו, וכורך החלק על כל ההיקף:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:12:2.english: And its end [should be] enough to wrap around [the scroll's] circumference - At its end, he leaves a large blank section, in order to wrap with it the entire circumference [of the scroll]. For he does not make two rollers [i.e., two poles] to roll it toward its middle, as we do with a Torah scroll; rather, he rolls it from its beginning to its end, and wraps the [blank] section around the whole circumference.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:1:1.hebrew: קח לך עבדים - שיחממו אותו, ורחוץ בו. ולא מצי עני למימר ליה: קנה חלקי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:1:1.english: Take for yourself slaves - who will heat it [the bathhouse], and wash in it. And a poor person cannot say to him, "Buy my share."

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:1:2.hebrew: הכא נמי גוד איכא, אגוד ליכא - שאין העני אומר לו: אף אני אקנה חלקך, שאין לו במה לקנות. לפיכך אין יכול לכופו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:1:2.english: Here too, there is "divide" but there is no "I will divide" - For the poor person cannot say to him, "I too will buy your share," since he has nothing with which to buy. Therefore, he cannot compel him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:2:1.hebrew: ושמו עליו - כל דבר שיש בו שיעור, שאם תחלקנו עדיין יהא עליו שמו הראשון:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:2:1.english: And its name remains upon it - Any item that has a measure, such that if you divide it, it will still have its original name.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:2:2.english: We raise it in price - That is, [the procedure of] "divide [it] or I will divide [it]" (gud o agud).

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:2:3.hebrew: טול אתה שיעור ואני פחות - כגון חצר שאין בה שמנה אמות, ואמר זה: חלוק, וטול לך ד' אמות, ואני המותר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:2:3.english: You take the minimum measure, and I [will take] less - For example, a courtyard that does not have eight cubits [of space], and this one said: Divide [it], and you take four cubits for yourself, and I [will take] the remainder.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:3:1.hebrew: וגוד או אגוד נמי - שלא רצה למחול כלום, אלא: קנה חלקי, או אקנה חלקך:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:3:1.english: And "divide [it] or I will divide [it]" as well - For he did not want to forgo anything, but [says]: Buy my share, or I will buy your share.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:1.hebrew: הא דרב יהודה - דאמר "גוד או אגוד" משמיה דרביה, קבלה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:1.english: This [statement] of Rav Yehuda - That he said "Divide or I will divide," in the name of his teacher, [is] a received tradition.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:2.hebrew: בכרך אחד - כל ספריהן עשויין בגליון, ואם יביאהו לב"ד לחלקו — בזיון הוא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:2.english: In one scroll - All their books are made on a single parchment sheet, and if he brings it to the court to divide it, it is a disgrace.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:3.hebrew: אבל בשתי כריכות - כגון תורה בכרך אחד, ונביאים בכרך אחד:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:3.english: But in two bindings - For example, the Torah in one volume and the Prophets in one volume.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:4.hebrew: חולקין - קס"ד דאפילו אין שניהם רוצים, וע"כ אין דמיהן שוין, ואי לית דינא דגוד או אגוד, היאך הוא כופיהו? זה יאמר: אני לא אתן לך עודף הדמים, וגם לא אתן לך היפה שאקבל ממך דמים. ולא גרסי' תרוייהו צריכין להאי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:5:4.english: They divide - It enters one's mind [that this applies] even if the two do not want [to divide], and [that] necessarily their values are not equal. And if there is no law of "either sell or buy" (gud o agud), how can he compel them? This one will say, "I will not give you the surplus of the money, and I also will not give you the better [portion], [in return] for which I would receive money from you." And we do not read "both of them need this."

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:6:1.hebrew: בששניהם רוצים - הא דשמואל, אשניהם רוצים דמתניתין קאי, דקתני "לא יחלוקו", ואמר שמואל: בשתי כריכות, אם שניהם רוצים — יחלוקו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:6:1.english: When both of them want [to divide] - This statement of Shmuel refers to the case in the Mishnah of "both of them want [to divide]," where it teaches "they shall not divide." And Shmuel said: [In the case of] two scrolls, if both of them want, they may divide.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:7:1.hebrew: פילכא ונוולא - לטוות ולארוג. ל"א: ביסתרקי — תכשיטי ספסלים — שקורין טפי"ד:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:7:1.english: A spindle and a shuttle - For spinning and for weaving. Another explanation: bistraki are ornaments for benches, which are called tapid [tapis, in Old French].

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:7:2.hebrew: לית דינא דגוד או אגוד - לכופו לתת דמי העודפים ביפה, ולא למכור חלקו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:7:2.english: There is no law of "divide or I will divide" - to compel him to give the value of the excess in the better [portion], and not to sell his share.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:8:1.hebrew: לאו גוד או אגוד הוא - אי לא אמר ליה "או קח שתיהם או אקח שתיהם", דכל אחת אין בה כדי לאחד:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:8:1.english: It is not [a case of] "divide or I will divide" - If he did not say to him, "Either take both or I will take both," for each one [alone] does not have enough to be joined together.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:8:2.english: But with two scrolls, they divide - And we thought [this means] even against the will of one of them. Apparently, when he says to him, "Take one, and 'gud' [pay] the value of the extra ones, or I will 'agud'" [that is, "Take one and buy me out for the value of the extra ones, or I will buy you out"], we compel him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:9:1.hebrew: כל אחד ואחד בפני עצמו - כל ספר וספר של נביאים ושל כתובים צריך להיות כרך לעצמו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 13b:9:1.english: Each one by itself - Each and every book of the Prophets and of the Writings must be a separate volume by itself.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:11:1.hebrew: ומסיים מלמטה ומתחיל מלמעל' - פי' בקונטרס: ואינו צריך להניח ד' שיטין. ונראה לר"י דבין חומש לחומש של תורה צריך להניח, ואנביאים דוקא קאמר דאין צריך, כדמפרש טעמא לקמן שאם בא לחתוך חותך; אבל בין חומש לחומש של תורה לא, מידי דהוי אפרשה פתוחה שאם היה מסיים מלמטה היה צריך להניח שיטה אחת, הכא נמי דין הוא להניח בסוף כל חומש פרשה של ד' שיטין. וריצב"א מפרש: ומסיים מלמטה ומתחיל מלמעלה, ולעולם מניח ד' שיטין, ודוקא בין נביא לנביא, אבל בין חומש לחומש לא יסיים מלמטה ומתחיל מלמעלה אפי' בהנחת ד' שיטין, כדאמר בירושלמי בפ"ק דמגילה: "וצריך שיהא גומר באמצע הדף ומתחיל באמצעיתו, ובנביא מסיים בסופו ומתחיל בראשו כו'". ונראה לי הטעם: דאין לו לסיים בסוף הדף אפי' יניח ארבעה שיטין, משום שמא יבוא לחתוך; אבל בין נביא לנביא, שאם בא לחתוך חותך — מסיים מלמטה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:11:1.english: "And he finishes at the bottom and begins at the top" - Rashi explains in the Kuntres: And he does not need to leave four lines. But it appears to the Ri that between one book of the Torah and the next he must leave [four lines], and [the Baraita] said [that he need not] specifically with regard to the Prophets, for he does not need to, as [the Gemara] explains the reason below: that if he comes to cut [the scroll], he may cut it. But between one book of the Torah and the next, [this is] not [the case], just as with an open section (parashah petuchah), where if he were to finish at the bottom [of the column] he would need to leave one line; here too it is proper to leave a section of four lines at the end of each book. And the Rizba explains: [the Baraita means] "he finishes at the bottom and begins at the top," and he always leaves four lines, and this applies specifically between one Prophet and the next; but between one book of the Torah and the next, he should not finish at the bottom and begin at the top, even if he leaves four lines, as it says in the Yerushalmi in the first chapter of Megillah: "And he must finish in the middle of the page and begin in the middle of it, but with a Prophet he finishes at its end and begins at its beginning, etc." And it seems to me that the reason is: he should not finish at the end of the page, even if he leaves four lines, lest he come to cut [the scroll]; but between one Prophet and the next, where if he comes to cut he may cut, he finishes at the bottom.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:12:1.english: "And he makes at its beginning enough to roll a column, and at its end enough for the circumference" - So it is written in all the books [of the Gemara], and it is difficult for Rabbeinu Yitzchak (the Ri), for it is taught in Tractate Soferim: All scrolls are rolled to their beginning; and below [the Gemara] also says that the scroll of Ezra is rolled to its beginning. And what the Kuntres [Rashi] explained, "from its beginning to its end," the wording does not imply this. And regarding a mezuzah, too, we say that one winds it from the word "Echad" toward "Shema," which is [winding it] toward its beginning. And explicitly we read in the Yerushalmi, in the first chapter of Megillah: A person makes a column for a Torah scroll at its end. Therefore it appears to the Ri that the text reads: "And he makes at its beginning enough for the circumference, and at its end enough to roll a column." But to the Rashba it appears to retain the reading of the books [as they have it]. And here it is different, because [the baraita] is dealing with one who joins the Torah, Prophets, and Writings [together]; and in that case it is not proper to make a column at the end, as one does elsewhere, for it is disgraceful for the Torah to be wrapped around the Prophets and Writings, and it would appear as if it were made a protector for them against dirt. Therefore here he makes a column at its beginning, so that the Torah will be on the inside and the Prophets and Writings on the outside. And below, where [the Gemara] answers "it teaches [this] regarding the sides," [the Ri] does not read "the beginning of the book enough to roll a column and its end enough to roll the circumference," for there it is not dealing with one who joins the Torah, Prophets, and Writings, and we would have to say the opposite. And in most books [the text] reads only "it teaches [this] regarding the sides," and nothing more. Furthermore, the Rashba says that even according to the books that do read it, it is not so difficult, for it is preferable [for the Gemara] to answer in a manner similar to this baraita on which it is commenting.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:5:1.hebrew: ואי ס"ד לית דינא דגוד או אגוד אפי' בשתי כריכות כו' - השתא ס"ד דחולקין, כיון שאחד רוצה לחלוק, וב' כריכות דומיא דכרך אחד, שאין כתוב באחד מה שכתוב באחר, כגון יהושע ושמואל. ואמאי חולקין בע"כ? והא אינם שוין! אלא ודאי אית דינא דגוד או אגוד. וא"ת: אפילו אית דינא דגוד או אגוד, אמאי חולקין, כיון שכתוב בזה מה שאין בזה, ותרוייהו צריכי להאי ולהאי? וי"ל דהוי מצי למימר "וליטעמיך". ולא גרס הכא מה שכתוב במיעוט ספרים "ואי ס"ד לית ליה דינא דגוד או אגוד, כי היכי דתרוייהו צריכי להאי תרוייהו צריכי להאי", דהא כל שכן דאי לא צריכי תרוייהו להאי ולהאי, פריך טפי שפיר: אי לית ליה דינא דגוד או אגוד, אמאי חולקין?:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:5:1.english: "And if it enters your mind that there is no law of 'either sell or buy' (gud o agud), even with two scrolls, etc." - Now it enters [the Gemara's] mind that they divide [the scrolls], since one of them wants to divide, and two scrolls are comparable to one scroll, [for the case is] where what is written in one is not written in the other, such as Joshua and Samuel. And why do they divide against the will [of one of them]? But they are not equal! Rather, certainly there is a law of "gud o agud." And if you ask: Even if there is a law of "gud o agud," why do they divide, since what is written in this one is not in that one, and both of them need this one and that one? And one can answer that [the Gemara] could have said, "And according to your reasoning." And in this [passage] we do not have the reading that is found in a minority of books: "And if it enters your mind that he holds there is no law of 'gud o agud' — just as both need this one, both need that one," for all the more so, if both do not need this one and that one, the question is stronger and sounder: If he holds there is no law of "gud o agud," why do they divide?

Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:9:1.hebrew: מדביק אדם תורה נביאים וכתובים כאחד - אע"פ שא"א שלא יתן נביאים וכתובים על גבי תורה, ובמגילה בפ"ב (דף כז.) משמע דאסור להניח ה"מ בשתי כריכות; אבל כשהן מדובקין יחד — אינו גנאי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:9:1.english: A person may bind Torah, Prophets, and Writings together as one - Even though it is impossible not to place Prophets and Writings on top of the Torah, and in Megillah, chapter 2 (27a), it implies that it is forbidden to place these in two separate wrappings; but when they are bound together, it is not a disgrace.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:9:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר תורה בפני עצמה - לא מפני שאסור להניח זה על גב זה מצריך שיהא כל אחד בפני עצמו, דלא אשכחן שיהא אסור להניח אלא נביאים וכתובים על גבי תורה, אבל נביאים על גבי כתובים או איפכא לא. אלא היינו טעמא: שלא יראה הכל כמו תורה, או הכל נביאים, כי היכי דאמרי חכמים בתר הכי, דבעו שיהא כל נביא ונביא בפני עצמו. וע"כ טעמא שלא יהא נראה הכל כמו נביא אחד. כן נראה לרשב"א:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 13b:9:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the Torah by itself - [He requires that each one be by itself] not because it is forbidden to place one on top of another, for we do not find that placing is forbidden except [placing] Prophets and Writings on top of the Torah; but [placing] Prophets on top of Writings, or the reverse, [is] not [forbidden]. Rather, this is the reason: that it should not appear as though everything is [one] Torah, or everything is Prophets — just as the Sages say afterward, that they require each and every prophet to be by itself. And therefore the reason must be that it should not appear as though everything is one prophet. So it appears to the Rashba.
